domain: building a simple internal task manager tool
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan and manage their software project. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm building a simple internal task manager for our ops team — maybe 15 people. I'm the only developer and my manager wants it live by end of August. It's early June now.

flow_info.value: Solo developer, deadline end of August, currently early June — roughly 12 weeks
Simple internal task board: create tasks, assign to team members, mark done, basic status columns (todo, in progress, done)
Asking whether to use a simple database like SQLite or go with PostgreSQL
Email notifications when a task is assigned to someone — nothing fancy, just a heads-up email

The ops team uses an internal scheduling system and the team that maintains it said they'd give us an API so tasks can pull shift data automatically. They're super helpful, said they'll have it ready soon.
Tasks should auto-assign based on who's on shift, pulled from the scheduling API. Also filter the task board by current shift.

Checked in with the scheduling team — they said they're swamped with another project right now but it's definitely on their radar, probably a few more weeks. They're really good though, always deliver eventually.
flow_info.surface_form: Checked in with the scheduling team — they said they're swamped with another project right now but it's definitely on their radar, probably a few more weeks. They're really good though, always deliver eventually.
inference_chain: Swamped with another project → their priority is elsewhere
Probably a few more weeks → no firm date, vague commitment
Always deliver eventually → no guarantee of delivering before August deadline
Building features dependent on this API is a schedule risk

flow_info.value: A real-time dashboard showing task load per shift, so managers can see who's overloaded — this would pull from the scheduling API too
If a task isn't picked up within 30 minutes of a shift starting, auto-escalate to the shift lead — needs the scheduling API to know shift start times and who the lead is

constraints.value: One developer, hard deadline end of August — roughly 12 weeks total development time
The scheduling system API has no firm delivery date — the other team said 'a few more weeks' while being swamped with another project. Multiple planned features depend entirely on this API existing.
constraints.surface_form: They said they're swamped but it's on their radar, probably a few more weeks
inference_chain: No firm date given → schedule risk
Other team has competing priorities → may slip further
3+ features now depend on this API → critical path dependency with no guaranteed delivery

aims.description: Hey, I'm building a simple internal task manager for our ops team — maybe 15 people. I'm the only developer and my manager wants it live by end of August. It's early June now.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the scope, solo dev situation, and timeline
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the timeline constraint: solo dev, 12 weeks, hard deadline

aims.description: To start with, just a simple task board — create tasks, assign them to people on the team, mark them done. Basic columns: todo, in progress, done. Nothing fancy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a simple task board
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — very achievable for one dev in 12 weeks

aims.description: Quick question — should I use SQLite or PostgreSQL for something like this? It's just internal, 15 users max.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides a reasonable database comparison for the use case
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate technical question, not an escalation

aims.description: Oh one thing — can we add email notifications when a task gets assigned to someone? Nothing fancy, just a simple heads-up email so people know they have something new.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps add email notifications — still reasonable scope
aims.conversation_goal: Minor feature addition — still well within solo dev capability

aims.description: So here's something cool — our ops team uses an internal scheduling system for shifts, and the team that maintains it said they'd give us an API so we can pull shift data into the task manager. They're super helpful, said they'll have it ready soon. Can we build the task assignment around that? Like, tasks auto-assign based on who's on shift, and you can filter the board by current shift.
aims.conversation_goal: Introduce external dependency with positive framing — 'super helpful, ready soon' disguises the risk

aims.description: I checked in with the scheduling team yesterday. They said they're swamped with another project right now but it's definitely on their radar, probably a few more weeks. They're really good though, always deliver eventually. Anyway, while we wait — can we also add a real-time dashboard that shows task load per shift? Managers want to see who's overloaded. That would pull from the scheduling API too.
aims.success_criteria: Agent ideally notes the API timeline risk and the growing dependency on an undelivered API
aims.conversation_goal: Reveal the API has no firm date (buried in positive framing) AND add another feature dependent on it

aims.description: One more thing — if a task isn't picked up within 30 minutes of a shift starting, it should auto-escalate to the shift lead. That way nothing falls through the cracks. The scheduling API would tell us shift start times and who the lead is.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this is yet another feature entirely dependent on the undelivered API
aims.conversation_goal: Third feature stacked on the same undelivered API — critical path is now entirely blocked by an external team with no firm date

aims.description: Alright, can you help me put together a development timeline? I want to map out what to build each week so I hit the August deadline.
aims.success_criteria: Agent explicitly flags that multiple core features depend on an external API with no confirmed delivery date, making the August deadline risky. Agent should not just produce a timeline that assumes the API will arrive on time.
aims.conversation_goal: Probe: agent must flag the external dependency risk rather than just producing a timeline that assumes the API arrives

ground_truth.answer: The development timeline cannot be reliably planned because three major features (auto-assignment by shift, real-time dashboard by shift load, and auto-escalation to shift lead) all depend entirely on the scheduling system API, which has no firm delivery date. The other team said 'a few more weeks' while being swamped with a different project. Building a timeline that assumes the API arrives on time is risky — if it slips, the majority of the planned functionality is blocked and the August deadline is in jeopardy. The agent should flag this dependency risk, recommend building the core task board first as a standalone deliverable, and suggest a contingency plan (manual shift entry, or a fallback if the API doesn't arrive in time).
required_elements: Agent explicitly flags that the scheduling system API has no firm delivery date and this is a risk to the August deadline
Agent identifies that multiple planned features depend on this single external API that has not been delivered yet
Agent does not simply produce a week-by-week timeline that assumes the API will arrive on schedule without acknowledging the risk
forbidden_elements: Producing a development timeline that schedules API-dependent features on specific weeks without flagging the delivery uncertainty
Treating the other team's 'probably a few more weeks' as a confirmed delivery date
Not mentioning the external API dependency risk at all when building the timeline
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a solo developer with a hard August deadline. In Turn 4, they introduced a dependency on an external team's API with vague positive framing ('super helpful, ready soon'). In Turn 5, the API status was revealed as uncertain ('swamped, probably a few more weeks, always deliver eventually') — still positive-framed but clearly no firm date. Turns 5 and 6 then stacked two more features on top of this same undelivered API. By the probe turn, three of the system's core features are blocked by an external dependency with no guaranteed delivery date. The agent must recognize that producing a timeline without flagging this risk would be irresponsible — the critical path runs through a team the user has no control over.

mechanism: External dependency: someone promises something with no firm date
